title.en: Grand-Pré · Working a tidal landscape and forced displacement
title.zh: 大普雷 · 潮汐景观中的劳动与强制迁移

location.label: Grand-Pré, Minas Basin; representative Acadian farming and commemorative landscape

summary.en:
Acadian settlement around Grand-Pré expanded from the early 1680s on the shores of the Minas Basin. Families built dykes and drainage works to turn tidal marsh into farmland. The aboiteau drainage system and the coordinated maintenance of embankments made collective work part of agricultural life. This landscape was produced through institutions and labour, rather than existing as an empty stage for imperial events.

Surplus crops and cattle connected the community with other Atlantic settlements. Yet distance from colonial capitals did not insulate it from competing French and British military projects. In 1755 British authorities began forcibly deporting Acadians. Parks Canada distinguishes the removals from Les Mines that year from the wider deportation continuing to 1762. Those administrative dates do not imply that every family followed the same itinerary or experienced a single moment of departure.

Acadians were permitted to return to Nova Scotia in 1764, but former lands had been occupied by New England Planters and return did not restore the earlier community unchanged. The surviving agricultural landscape and later memorials carry different histories. Twentieth-century monuments and the 2012 World Heritage inscription commemorate and interpret that past; they are not dates of Acadian arrival or evidence that displacement ended cultural life.
summary.zh:
阿卡迪亚家庭自十七世纪八十年代初在米纳斯湾岸边扩大大普雷聚落，修筑堤坝与排水设施，把潮汐盐沼变成农田。以水闸排水的aboiteau系统及共同维护堤防的工作，使集体协作成为农业生活的一部分。这一景观由制度与劳动塑造，并非帝国事件发生前的一片空白舞台。

剩余谷物与牲畜使社群同大西洋沿岸其他聚落相连，但远离殖民首府并不意味着能够避开英法军事竞争。1755年英国当局开始强制驱逐阿卡迪亚人。加拿大公园局区分了当年莱米讷地区的驱逐与持续至1762年的更广泛驱逐过程；这些行政年代不代表所有家庭都遵循相同行程或在同一天离开。

1764年当局准许阿卡迪亚人返回新斯科舍，但故土已由新英格兰移民占据，返回并未原样恢复旧社群。存续农业景观与后来的纪念物承载着不同历史。二十世纪纪念建筑及2012年世界遗产列名是在纪念和解释过去，不是阿卡迪亚人抵达的日期，也不表示流离使其文化终结。

dateNote.en: 1682–1764 selects settlement, deportation and permission to return. Dates are not the lifespan of Acadian culture, nor a claim that every dyke was constructed in 1682.
dateNote.zh: 1682—1764年选取聚居、驱逐与准许返回的过程；不是阿卡迪亚文化的起止，也不表示每座堤坝都建于1682年。

title.en: African Nova Scotians · Slavery, freedom and the surviving record
title.zh: 非裔新斯科舍人 · 奴役、自由与存世记录

location.label: Halifax; representative colonial port and administrative context, not all African Nova Scotian communities

summary.en:
African Nova Scotian history includes enslavement, migration and the work of building communities under unequal conditions. Nova Scotia Archives selects 1749–1834 for its documentary exhibition because these dates connect Halifax’s founding with the coming into effect of British colonial abolition legislation. The archive explicitly warns that neither African presence nor slavery began with Halifax in 1749. The selected dates also reflect which documents survive in its holdings.

The Book of Negroes records Black people leaving New York with British evacuation in 1783. Names, descriptions and statements about freedom were entered within a military and administrative process. Reading such a register can recover individual lives, but an official entry is not a complete autobiography or independent proof of every assertion it contains.

The wider exhibition brings household, labour and settlement evidence into view, including a Black woodcutter portrayed at Shelburne in 1788. These materials complicate any account in which moving north automatically secured equality. Halifax is a navigational reference for the colonial port and administrative setting; it does not collapse Birchtown, Preston, Shelburne or other communities into one place. Later photographs describe continuities beyond the chosen interval rather than implying that community history ended in 1834.
summary.zh:
非裔新斯科舍人的历史包含奴役、迁移，以及在不平等条件下建立社群的劳动。新斯科舍档案馆为其文献展选取1749—1834年，把哈利法克斯建立与英国殖民地废奴法律生效相连。档案馆明确提醒：非裔人的存在与奴隶制都不是1749年建城时才出现。所选年代也反映该馆保存了哪些文献。

《黑人名册》记录了1783年随英国撤离而离开纽约的黑人。姓名、年龄、体貌及有关自由身份的说法，被纳入军事与行政登记程序。阅读名册能够追索个人生命，但官方条目既非完整自传，也不独立证明其中每项陈述。

更广的展览呈现家庭、劳动与聚居证据，包括1788年谢尔本一位黑人伐木工的图像。这些材料使“北迁自动带来平等”的叙述难以成立。哈利法克斯仅是殖民港口与行政环境的导航参照，不把伯奇敦、普雷斯顿、谢尔本等社群压成同一个地点。较晚照片说明所选时段之后的延续，而非暗示社群历史于1834年终结。

dateNote.en: 1749–1834 is the archive exhibition’s selected documentary window, not the beginning/end of Black presence or community life. The1783 register concerns departure from New York; the Halifax point is not its place of creation.
dateNote.zh: 1749—1834年是档案展选定的文献时段，并非非裔存在或社群生活的起止。1783年名册涉及从纽约离开；哈利法克斯点不是名册的制作地点。
